      Engineering research

      De Stellaris Wiki
      Ir a la navegación Ir a la búsqueda

      Version

      This article has been verified for the current PC version (4.5) of the game.

      Technology

      Technology
      Physics research
      Society research
      Engineering research

      Engineering is one of the three research areas. It consists of the following fields:

      • Industry: mineral production, robotics, building construction, cosmic storm protection.
      • Materials: armor, industrial buildings, strategic resources.
      • Propulsion: kinetic and explosive weapons, thrusters.
      • Voidcraft: ship types and hulls, starbases, strike craft, megastructures.

      Table usage[editar | editar código]

      Color indicators: Starter, Acquisition, Rare, Dangerous, Repeatable.

      Notes:

      1. The table shows the default names/icons of techs. Flavor entry is displayed if accompanied by a change to effects/requirements.
      2. If a tech was available as a research option as part of the last choice, then its (total) weight is halved in the coming choice.
      3. The table denotes the base cost of a tech. Actual in-game tech cost scales with game settings and (number of colonized planets and population).
      4. To research techs of higher tiers, it is necessary to first acquire six or more techs of the preceding tier.
      5. Sorting the table by tiers places all Starter tech at the top and Repeatable end-game tech at the bottom.
      6. Most icons also double as links. For more information about an unlocked effect (buildings, components, etc.), click on the accompanying icon.

      Our society need not be limited to one home. With the ability to construct additional Arkships, every direction becomes a path, and every path becomes ours.

If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

      These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms.
